With each bag purchased, a donation is made to the Pink Boots Society scholarship fund in the US and Canada to support their mission: to assist, inspire and encourage women and non-binary individuals in the fermented/alcoholic beverage industry.

entries.name: Premium Two Row Malt
entries.description: Classic. Premium. Perfection. For generations, Premium Two Row has been our pinnacle base malt. It’s perfect for all beer styles, especially American ales and lagers, producing a very clean, smooth finish. When you want peak performance, there’s no better choice than our Premium Two Row.
entries.notes: Premium Two Row is produced from Western U.S. barley, this base malt is processed meticulously to create a balanced flavor profile designed to be at the heart of your craft.

entries.name: Pure Idaho Pilsner Malt
entries.description: Between the rugged Sawtooth Mountains and craggy Grand Tetons lie golden fields of barley perfection. It’s here, to the West of the Great Divide, where we craft our renowned Pure Idaho malt.
entries.notes: 100% Idaho-grown barley. This unique pilsner malt is fully-modified and gently dried. It contributes a light color and balanced flavor profile designed to be at the heart of your craft.

entries.name: Pure Oregon Malt
entries.description: From the center of the craft brewing revolution comes the malt at the heart of it all: Pure Oregon. Crafted from 100% Oregon barley, it’s what makes a true Oregon brew.
entries.notes: 100% Oregon-grown barley. This special base malt is fully-modified and gently dried. It contributes a balanced flavor profile designed to be at the heart of your craft.

entries.name: Pure Washington Malt
entries.description: In the sunset shadow of the Cascade Range grows some of the finest barley in North America. Welcome to the Palouse: God’s country, where deep, rich soil and a perfect climate converge to create the Pure Washington malt you love.
entries.notes: 100% Washington-grown barley. This special base malt is fully-modified and gently dried. It contributes a balanced flavor profile designed to be at the heart of your craft.

entries.name: Superior Pilsen Malt
entries.description: As crisp and clean as fresh mountain air, this two row pilsner malt is simply superior. It’s perfect for brewing the malty, light-colored lagers and ales we all crave after a hearty day in the great outdoors.
entries.notes: Superior Pilsen malt is produced with care and a gentle processing regime. By utilizing lower protein barley and a delicate kilning program, we are able to create a fully functional base malt with accentuated extract and low color formation.

entries.name: Vienna Malt
entries.description: Craftsmanship. That’s what it takes to make outstanding malt and beer alike. It’s why brewers have relied on our Vienna malt to be at the heart of their craft for generations.
entries.notes: Vienna malt is created with attention to flavor development and malt complexity. Great for brewing full-bodied beers with rich malt and light biscuit characteristics.

entries.name: White Wheat Malt
entries.description: Hearty enough to withstand a Pacific Northwest winter, White Wheat is steeped, germinated and kilned to perfection. It’s the premium choice for American wheat beers.
entries.notes: Our White Wheat malt is grown exclusively in the Pacific Northwest. Fully malted and kilned to develop soft balanced sweetness, high extract and a light bready flavor. Great for foam retention.

entries.name: White Wheat Unmalted
entries.description: Grown in the Pacific Northwest, Unmalted White Wheat is carefully cleaned and graded after harvest. This bag contains only the finest raw white wheat, excellent for body and retaining haze in your beer.
entries.notes: Grown exclusively in the Pacific Northwest, Unmalted White Wheat will provide additional body and foam stability. It contributes desirable cloudiness to Belgian and hazy beer styles.

entries.name: 5 Lovibond Golden Belgian Candi Syrup
entries.description: 5 Lovibond Golden Belgian Candi Syrup Golden Candi Syrup is an unparalleled, superior quality rich golden syrup. Golden is a rich translucent 24 karat gold and adds a pronounced caramel and light fruit palate to authentic Belgian Tripels, Saisons, Golden Ales, and Bier de Garde.

entries.name: Belgian Candi Syrup - Extra Dark
entries.description: Extra Dark Belgian Candi Syrup The richest, darkest Belgian candi syrup. Imparts hints of dark raisin and extra dark stone fruit on top of a roasty, dark caramel palate. Superb for Belgian style ales and brew that need a full body and indescribable flavor. SRM 240

entries.name: Blonde Soft Candi Sugar
entries.description: Soft Blonde Candi Sugar (Geel) Soft Blonde Candi Sugar (Geel) is the ideal addition for homebrewers crafting Belgian ales, Tripels, and Belgian Blondes. Its delicate caramelized sugar, honey-like sweetness, and subtle aromatic complexity elevate your brews authentically. Made from premium beet and cane sugars, it's non-GMO, gluten-free, and vegan-friendly. Boost your ABV, achieve exceptional flavor balance, and bring authentic Belgian character to your homebrew recipes. Blonde Candi Sugar Key Features: Color: 85–175 EBC (approximately 32–66 SRM), soft gold to light amber Flavor: Subtle caramel, confectionary sweetness Saccharose Content: Minimum 94.5% Moisture: ≤ 2.5% Extract Potential: 1.046 SG per pound per gallon (46 PPG) Dietary Suitability: Gluten-free, Non-GMO, Vegan Blonde Candi Sugar Brewing Suggestions: Ideal for Belgian ales, Tripels, Belgian Blondes, and other styles.

entries.name: Brown Soft Candi Sugar
entries.description: Soft Brown Candi Sugar (Bruin) Soft Brown Candi Sugar (Bruin) brings complexity, depth, and authentic Belgian flavor to your dubbels, quadrupels, and specialty dark ales. Crafted from select beet and cane sugars, this brewing sugar imparts rich molasses, caramel undertones, and mild dark-fruit notes of raisin and plum. Ideal for increasing fermentability and deepening flavor without excessive sweetness. Gluten-free, vegan, and non-GMO./p> Brown Candi Sugar Key Features: Color: 410–710 EBC (approximately 155–268 SRM), deep amber to dark brown Flavor: Rich molasses, mild dark fruit (raisin, plum), caramel Saccharose Content: Minimum 94.5% Moisture: ≤ 2.5% Extract Potential: 1.046 SG per pound per gallon (46 PPG) Dietary Suitability: Gluten-free, Non-GMO, Vegan Brown Candi Sugar Brewing Suggestions: Perfect for Belgian-style dubbels, quadrupels, dark ales, and other specialty beers, adding complexity and character without overpowering sweetness.

entries.name: Clear Belgian Candi Sugar
entries.description: Imported from Belgium, this sugar is refined from sugar beets, and is 100% fermentable. 0°L.

entries.name: D-180 Candi Syrup
entries.description: D-180 is a premium extra dark Belgian candi syrup is perfect for use in dark Belgian ales. This premium extra dark Belgian candi syrup has deep flavors of fresh ground coffee, dark fruit, and toasted bread. Perfect for use in dark Belgian ales. 180 SRM, 1.032 PPG.

entries.name: D-45 Candi Syrup
entries.description: This premium amber Belgian candi syrup is perfect for amber and brown Belgian ales. The syrup has flavors of toffee, vanilla, and toasted bread. 45 SRM, 1.032 PPG.

entries.name: D-90 Candi Syrup
entries.description: This premium dark candi syrup creates subtle chocolate, toffee, and toasted bread flavors in dark Belgian ales. D-90 is a versatile dark candi syrup. This syrup creates an unmistakable and subtle chocolate back-palate, toffee, and toasted bread flavors.

entries.name: Dark Belgian Candi Sugar
entries.description: Imported from Belgium, this sugar is refined from sugar beets, and is 100% fermentable. Rated at 275°L; actual color contribution is lower.

entries.name: Simplicity Candi Syrup
entries.description: A premium clear Belgian candi syrup made from beet sugar. Provides clean honey-like flavor to light Belgian Ales. Great for Tripels, Golden Strong ales, or anytime you're looking for increased drinkability and complexity. 0 SRM, 1.032 ppg.

entries.name: Amber Malt
entries.description:
Amber Malt is a lightly roasted malt that delivers toasty, biscuity and dry nutty flavours, with a warm copper-brown hue (54-71 °EBC).

Our most versatile roasted malt, it adds depth, dryness and subtle roastiness without excessive bitterness, making it ideal for Bitters, Milds, Porters, Brown Ales and Stouts and other historical recipes where a crisp, toasty malt backbone is desired.

Compared to our highly kilned malts, Amber Malt is drier and more biscuity, offering less sweetness and more toastiness.

Typically used at 5-20% in the grist, Amber Malt enhances complexity and dryness, balancing sweeter caramel malts while adding a distinctive toasted, biscuity depth. It’s a great choice for brewers looking to introduce traditional malt character with a crisp, slightly roasted edge.
entries.notes: Biscuit, Dry

entries.name: Aromatic Malt
entries.description:
Aromatic Malt is a highly kilned, intensely flavourful malt that delivers rich, malty depth with deep amber to copper hues (50-70 °EBC). It boasts strong toasty, honeyed and slightly caramelised notes, with a pronounced malty-sweet aroma that enhances body and complexity in a range of styles from Belgian Dubbels to rich Amber Ales.

Compared to Imperial Malt, Aromatic Malt is sweeter and more aromatic, with less dryness and more pronounced malt richness.

Typically used at 5-20% in grists to boost malt character and aroma, it can contribute a rich malt backbone without overwhelming the beer. When used in smaller amounts, it adds depth and complexity, making it an excellent choice for brewers looking to enhance malt-forward beers with a warm, aromatic malt presence.
entries.notes: Malty, Honey, Raisins, Complex Sweetness with Sour After-Notes

entries.name: Best Pale Ale Malt
entries.description:
Best Pale Ale Malt is the foundation of characterful, full-bodied ales, offering a rich, bready malt backbone with a signature biscuity sweetness.

Kilned slightly higher than standard pale malts, it deepens in colour (4-6 °EBC), contributing a warm golden hue to the final beer.

The malt’s gentle toasty undertones and hints of light caramel provide depth, while its clean, well-rounded profile supports both hop-forward and malt-driven styles. Its balanced fermentability ensures a satisfying mouthfeel without excessive residual sweetness.

This malt excels in traditional and modern Pale Ales, Bitters, ESBs and IPAs, where its pronounced malt presence can stand up to bold hop character. It also enhances Golden Ales, Porters and even darker styles when layered for complexity. Brewers seeking depth without overwhelming sweetness will appreciate its versatility.
entries.notes: Rich Malty

entries.name: Black Malt
entries.description:
Black Malt is a heavily roasted malt that imparts intense roasted, burnt and coffee-like flavours without imparting too much astringency.

As well as a deep black hue (1433-1900 °EBC), Black Malt adds a strong, dry bitterness and bold roasted character, making it ideal for Porters, Stouts and other intensely dark beers where a pronounced roasted malt presence is desired.

Typically used up to 5% in the grist, Black Malt is perfect for brewers looking to enhance deep colour and add complexity to dark beers, while it can potentially be used as a handy colour adjuster in very small amounts in lighter beers.
entries.notes: Cocoa, Neutral

entries.name: Brown Malt
entries.description:
Brown Malt is a deeply toasted speciality malt that delivers rich roasted biscuit, nutty coffee and cocoa flavours, with a warm brown hue (400-508 °EBC).

It adds depth, dryness and a roasted complexity, making it an excellent choice for Porters, Stouts and Milds, where a toasty, coffee-like backbone without harsh bitterness is desired.

Compared to Amber Malt (54-71 °EBC), Brown Malt is darker, with a more pronounced roasted edge, while being less bitter than Pale Chocolate Malt (535-669 °EBC).

Typically used up to 10% in the grist, Brown Malt enhances body and malt complexity, providing a historical depth and warmth to traditional dark ales while remaining balanced and smooth.
entries.notes: Coffee Beans

entries.name: CaraGlow
entries.description:
CaraGlow is our lightest colour caramalt (10-20 °EBC), designed to deliver subtle sweetness, a very delicate malt flavour and a touch of fruity brightness, all while maintaining a clean, refreshing finish.

Its incredibly gentle crystallisation in one of our roasting drums produces a mild malty character with hay-like notes and aroma. This makes it suited to Pale Ales, Blonde Ales and Hazy IPAs, where a light touch of caramel complexity and improved mouthfeel are desired.

Compared to our standard Caramalt (30–42 °EBC), CaraGlow is lighter in both colour and flavour intensity, offering a cleaner, fresher profile.

Ideally, CaraGlow is used at 5-15% to add a slight fullness on the palate and a gentle sweetness, all without overshadowing hop or yeast character, making it perfect for brewers seeking nuance and finesse in lighter beer styles.
entries.notes: Mild Malty, Grassy, Hay

entries.name: Caramalt
entries.description:
Caramalt is a lightly caramelised malt that enhances beers with a delicate sweetness, subtle toffee notes and a smooth, rounded mouthfeel.

With a pale golden hue (30-42 °EBC), it provides gentle caramel and honey-like flavours without overpowering the beer’s balance. It’s perfect for light beers such as Pale Ales, Hazy IPAs and Blonde Ales, where a touch of body and malt complexity is desired.

Compared to our wider crystal malt range, Caramalt is light, soft and more fermentable, contributing sweetness and mouthfeel rather than heavy caramel or raisin-like flavours.

Typically used at 5-15% in grists, it enhances body and malt richness while keeping the beer’s profile bright and drinkable. It’s an excellent choice for brewers looking to soften hop bitterness and create a smooth, slightly sweet malt backbone.
entries.notes: Grassy, Mild Toffee, Sweet

entries.name: Chit Malt
entries.description:
Chit Malt is a very lightly germinated malt designed to boost foam stability, body and mouthfeel without contributing significant colour or flavour (max. 3.5 °EBC).

Retaining much of the raw barley's protein and enzyme content, it is ideal for modern beer styles like Hazy IPAs, New England IPAs and unfiltered Lagers, where enhanced haze, head retention and structure are key.

Unlike Dextrin Malt, which adds unfermentable sugars and a subtle sweetness, Chit Malt is less sweet, more functional and excels in delivering body-building proteins and haze-positive compounds with minimal impact on grist colour or flavour.

Typically used at 3-10% of the grist, Chit Malt is perfect for brewers seeking to enhance mouthfeel and foam in lighter or hop-forward styles, while maintaining a clean, fermentable base.
entries.notes: Neutral

entries.name: Chocolate Malt
entries.description:
Chocolate Malt is a roasted malt that imparts rich cocoa, dark coffee and roasted nut flavours along with a stunning dark brown hue (1067-1300 °EBC).

It contributes bold roastiness and a smooth bitterness, making it perfect for Porters, Stouts, Black Ales and other dark beers where a strong roasted malt character is desired.

Chocolate Malt offers a more intense roast flavour with deeper cocoa and coffee notes than Pale Chocolate, which contributes to a darker, fuller bitterness.

Typically used at up to 10% in the grist, Chocolate Malt brings dark, roasty complexity to a wide range of beers, enhancing colour and depth while balancing sweetness with a clean, roasted bitterness. It's a good choice for brewers looking for a rich, dark malt presence without overwhelming the beer.
entries.notes: Dark Chocolate

entries.name: Crystal Dark
entries.description:
Crystal Dark is a bold, intensely crystalised malt where we get into the delicious realms of complex toffee, dark fruit and burnt sugar, but without the astringency of roasted malt.

With those flavours combined with a rich, ruby-brown hue (250-285 °EBC), it makes Crystal Dark a perfect choice for Porters, Stouts and Barleywines, where a fuller caramel depth and darker malt character are desired.

Typically used at 5-15% in the grist, Crystal Dark provides a deep malt backbone, balancing hop bitterness while enhancing colour, body and layered caramel complexity, making it an essential malt for brewers aiming for depth and richness in darker beer styles.
entries.notes: Raisins, Toffee Sweetness, Burnt Caramel

entries.name: Crystal Dark Medium
entries.description:
Crystal Dark Medium is a bold, intensely crystalised malt that imparts hints of toffee, dark caramel and dried fruit notes, along with a deep amber to ruby hue (190-225 °EBC).

It enhances body, mouthfeel and malt complexity, making it ideal for Red Ales, Porters and Stouts, where a deeper caramel sweetness and colour contribution is desired.

Compared to Crystal Medium (167-190 °EBC), Crystal Dark Medium offers more intense caramelisation and a richer, deeper sweetness, with the first hints of light burnt sugar complexity. It remains less intense than Crystal Dark (200-250 °EBC), which leans more toward darker toffee and light roasted notes.

Typically used at 5-15% in the grist, Crystal Dark Medium provides a full, warming malt backbone, balancing hop bitterness with layers of toffee, caramelised sugar and subtle dark fruit complexity – perfect for brewers looking to add depth and richness without overpowering roastiness.
entries.notes: Dark Caramel, Hints of Toffee

entries.name: Crystal Extra Dark
entries.description:
Crystal Extra Dark is a highly crystalised, intensely flavourful malt that brings bold toffee, burnt sugar and dried fruit notes, along with a deep mahogany-brown hue (450-500 °EBC).

It adds rich malt complexity, body and depth, making it ideal for Stouts, Porters and Barleywines, where a robust caramel backbone and dark fruit sweetness are desired.

While it adds deep caramel complexity, it remains less bitter and roasted than the likes of Black Malt, making it perfect for brewers who want dark malt richness without acrid or charred flavours.

Typically used at no more than 10% in the grist, Crystal Extra Dark enhances colour, head retention, body and lingering sweetness, balancing roasted malts and hop bitterness with a warming, full-bodied malt presence.
entries.notes: Raisins, Christmas Cake

entries.name: Crystal Light
entries.description:
Crystal Light is a delicate crystal malt that delivers gentle toffee, honeyed sweetness and light dried fruit notes, alongside a rich golden-amber hue (95-113 °EBC).

It enhances body, mouthfeel and malt complexity, making it ideal for malt-forward ales and Bitters, where a balanced caramel sweetness and light colour enhancement are desired.

Crystal Light has a bright, clean sweetness, without the deeper toffee or burnt sugar notes of darker crystal malts.

Typically used at 5-15% in the grist, Crystal Light adds subtle malt complexity and residual sweetness while allowing hop and yeast character to shine through, making it a versatile choice for brewers seeking delicate caramel undertones without overpowering the beer.
entries.notes: Nutty, Dried Fruit, Biscuit

entries.name: Crystal Medium
entries.description:
Crystal Medium is a rich, deeply crystalised malt that imparts pronounced toffee, burnt sugar and light raisin-like notes, along with a warm copper-red hue (167-190 °EBC).

It enhances body, mouthfeel and malt complexity, making it a key ingredient in Bitters, Red Ales, Brown Ales and Porters, where colour depth and deeper caramel notes are desired, without edging into roasted or burnt sugar flavours.

Typically used at 5-15% in the grist, Crystal Medium is perfect for brewers looking to add depth, colour and residual sweetness, balancing hop bitterness with a rounded, toffee-like malt backbone.
entries.notes: Pronounced Caramel, Toffee Sweetness

entries.name: Crystal T50™
entries.description:
Crystal T50 (Target 50 Lovibond) is a mid-range crystal malt with a super tight spec. The malt is designed to provide balanced caramel sweetness, light toffee notes, a rich golden-amber hue and was developed following a request from one of the world’s leading breweries.

It enhances body, mouthfeel and malt complexity, making it ideal for Bitters, Pale Ales and Amber Ales, where a touch of caramel depth is needed without overwhelming the beer.

Typically used at 5-15% in the grist, Crystal T50 provides a smooth caramel character with a clean finish, making it a go-to malt for brewers seeking balanced sweetness and malt complexity without excessive residual sugar.
entries.notes: Honey, Mild Toffee, Delicate Malty Notes

entries.name: Dextrin Malt
entries.description:
Dextrin Malt is a handy little tool to keep up your sleeve – a speciality malt designed to enhance body, mouthfeel and foam stability, while imparting a subtle malty sweetness without adding colour (max 3.5 °EBC).

It is perfect in beers where a fuller texture and improved head retention are desired without altering the beer’s flavour balance. Specifically, it is useful in very light, hop forward IPAs to balance bitterness, while it’s also great in lower attenuated sweet beers, such as a Mild and Sweet Stout.

Typically used at 3-10% in the grist, Dextrin Malt is an excellent choice for brewers looking to enhance body and mouthfeel in lighter beers or create a smoother, fuller drinking experience in any style, all without affecting final gravity or sweetness too dramatically.
entries.notes: Neutral

entries.name: Export Pale Brown
entries.description:
Export Pale Brown is a much lighter take on our traditional Brown Malt, kilned to a colour range of 95-120 °EBC. This makes it an excellent choice for brewers seeking the biscuity, nutty and lightly toasted qualities of Brown Malt, but with a more restrained roast character and a cleaner finish.

Compared to Brown Malt (400.9-508.1 °EBC), Export Pale Brown offers far less acrid bitterness or intense dry roast, making it more versatile in a wider variety of styles where balance is key.

Expect warm cereal tones, subtle coffee and hints of dry cocoa, with less assertiveness on the palate than darker roasted malts. It brings a pleasant depth to Brown Ales, Milds and Porters when used at 5–15%, depending on the desired intensity.

Export Pale Brown is ideal where toasty malt complexity is desired without overpowering darker, more robust flavours.
entries.notes: Dry Cocoa, Subtle Coffee, Toasty

entries.name: Extra Pale Ale Malt
entries.description:
Extra Pale Ale Malt is a highly versatile, low-colour base malt designed for brewers seeking a clean, delicate malt backbone that allows hops and speciality ingredients to shine.

Kilned at a lower temperature than Best Pale Ale Malt, it delivers a lighter colour (max 3.5 °EBC), making it ideal for pale, hop-forward styles like West Coast IPAs, Hazy IPAs and crisp Golden Ales. Its flavour is subtle yet refined, with gentle sweet biscuit notes and a touch of fresh grain character.

Compared to Golden Promise, Extra Pale Ale offers a crisper, drier finish with less perceived sweetness while, against Maris Otter, it is lighter in colour and body, with a cleaner malt profile and higher fermentability.

In comparison to Best Pale Ale, meanwhile, Extra Pale Ale prioritises brightness and drinkability, making it perfect for modern, vibrant beer styles where clarity and hop expression are key.
entries.notes: Light Malty

entries.name: Finest Lager Malt
entries.description:
Finest Lager Malt is a premium, low-colour malt (max 3.5 °EBC) crafted for clean, crisp and delicate lagers.

With a light, straw-coloured hue and a soft, bready malt sweetness, it provides a balanced, neutral base that allows subtle yeast and hop characteristics to shine.

Its high modification and excellent enzymatic power ensure efficient mash conversion, making it a reliable choice for both traditional and modern lager styles, including Pilsners, Helles, Kölsch and light Continental-style beers.

Finest Lager lacks the richer malt character of Best Pale Ale or Maris Otter, offering a leaner, more delicate profile suited to highly attenuated, refreshing beers. If you're crafting a beer where crispness and subtlety are key, this malt provides the perfect foundation.
entries.notes: Light Malty, Fresh

entries.name: Finest Pale Ale Golden Promise®™
entries.description:
Finest Pale Ale Golden Promise® is a heritage malt known for its sweet, clean and slightly nutty malt character.

It delivers a well-rounded, balanced body with a touch of honeyed sweetness and a light golden hue (typically 4-6 °EBC). This malt – produced from heritage barley variety Golden Promise, which dates to the 1960s – is highly versatile, excelling in Pale Ales, IPAs, Bitters and Scotch Ales, where a smooth yet distinctive malt backbone is desired.

Compared to Best Pale Ale Malt, Finest Pale Ale Golden Promise® is slightly softer and sweeter, with a rounder mouthfeel and less pronounced biscuit notes and, against Maris Otter, it is cleaner, more delicate and offers a more refined sweetness.

Finest Pale Ale Golden Promise® also provides greater depth and malt complexity than Extra Pale Ale Malt, which is crisper and lighter in colour. Overall, this makes it a top choice for brewers seeking a high-quality, flavourful base malt with heritage.

Furthermore, as we own the Golden Promise variety, supply seed through our agricultural merchanting division and purchase the barley direct from trusted growers each year, we can offer full traceability and sustainability data on the finished malt.
entries.notes: Light Malty

entries.name: Finest Pale Ale Maris Otter
entries.description:
Finest Pale Ale Maris Otter Malt is a renowned British heritage malt prized for its rich, biscuity depth and full-bodied character.

It provides a warm golden hue (typically 4-6 °EBC) and a distinctively malty backbone, making it the go-to choice for classic British Ales, Bitters, ESBs, Porters and traditional IPAs.

Its well-rounded sweetness and slightly toasty undertones give beers a robust yet balanced malt presence, perfect for styles where malt complexity is key.

Compared to Finest Pale Ale Golden Promise®, Finest Pale Ale Maris Otter is more biscuity and bready, with a fuller mouthfeel and a slightly drier finish, while it is richer and more malty than Best Pale Ale, with a more pronounced toasty depth.

Overall, Finest Pale Ale Maris Otter brings a traditional, hearty malt character that remains largely unmatched for authentic, malt-forward British styles.
entries.notes: Rich Malty

entries.name: Finest Pot Still Golden Promise®
entries.description:
Finest Pot Still Golden Promise is a distilling malt produced from heritage UK two-row barley variety Golden Promise.

Golden Promise is renowned for its distinctively sweet, full-bodied flavour and unique balance of consistency and efficiency, making this product ideal for whisky distillers seeking characterful spirit yield with reliable performance.

While delivering good extract and spirit yields, Golden Promise contributes a rounder mouthfeel and a gentle malty sweetness to the new make spirit – qualities highly prized in premium single malt whisky production.

Compared to pot still malts made with modern two-row barley varieties, it brings a more traditional flavour profile, with subtle cereal, soft honey and creamy biscuity notes that shine through distillation and maturation. It’s ideal for distillers looking to add authenticity and richness to their spirit while maintaining efficient conversion and fermentation performance.

entries.name: Flaked Barley
entries.description:
Flaked Barley is an unmalted adjunct that brings a distinctive creamy mouthfeel and improved foam stability to a range of beer styles.

Produced by steaming and rolling barley into flat flakes, this ingredient contributes subtle grainy flavour, body and a smooth, velvety texture without introducing enzymatic activity.

It’s particularly valued in Stouts and Porters, where it helps develop that characteristic dense head and adds chewiness to the body.

Unlike malted barley, it won’t contribute fermentable sugars, but its starch content makes it ideal when mashed with a base malt high in diastatic power.

Typically used at rates of 5-20%, depending on the style and desired effect, Flaked Barley is an excellent tool for enhancing texture and visual appeal, becoming something of a go-to for traditional and contemporary dark beers alike.
entries.notes: Creamy

entries.name: Flaked Oats
entries.description:
Flaked Oats are a key ingredient in crafting smooth, creamy textures and enhancing mouthfeel in a variety of beer styles.

Produced by steaming and rolling whole oats, this adjunct adds a soft, smooth body and contributes to a rich, silky mouthfeel, making it a popular choice in Oatmeal Stouts, New England IPAs and Hazy Pale Ales.

Flaked Oats help improve head retention and contribute a mild, slightly sweet and nutty flavour profile. Typically used at 5-20%, they are particularly effective in increasing beer viscosity and enhancing the perception of fullness, especially in styles aiming for a fuller-bodied, soft drinking experience.

Unlike Malted Oats, which have enzymatic activity, Flaked Oats offer little fermentable sugar, making them ideal when mashed alongside highly diastatic base malts. They provide a more neutral, smooth flavour with less graininess, allowing the beer’s hops and malts to shine.
entries.notes: Neutral

entries.name: Flaked Wheat
entries.description:
Flaked Wheat is an unmalted adjunct prized for its ability to boost mouthfeel, body and head retention, particularly in hazy and wheat-forward beer styles.

Produced by steaming and rolling raw wheat, it retains high levels of proteins and gums that enhance foam stability and contribute to a soft, smooth texture.

Its flavour is clean and neutral, with a subtle grainy sweetness, making it a flexible addition in a wide range of beers – from traditional Belgian Witbiers to modern New England IPAs.

Typically used at 5-20% of the grist, it complements both base and speciality malts by improving body without overpowering the flavour profile.

Compared to Wheat Malt, Flaked Wheat has no enzymatic activity and contributes a more raw grainy character. It’s ideal when working with highly modified base malts and looking to introduce haze, creamy texture and stability without malt sweetness.
entries.notes: Neutral

entries.name: Golden Naked Oats®™
entries.description:
Golden Naked Oats is a unique, crystalised malt produced from a naked oat (no husk) that delivers silky mouthfeel, subtle nutty sweetness and delicious breakfast cereal flavours, with a deep golden-amber hue (12-24 °EBC).

Unlike our standard, husked Malted Oats, the crystalisation process develops deep caramelisation, making it an exceptional choice for Hazy IPAs, Stouts, Porters and malt-forward Ales, where it enhances body, head retention and smooth texture.

Its creaminess brings mouthfeel and balance to strong, hop forward beers and, although it is a similar colour to our CaraGlow and Caramalt products, Golden Naked Oats offers a more velvety texture with a softer, oat-driven sweetness.

Typically used at 5-15% in the grist, it adds depth, creaminess and a luscious malt complexity, making it an essential ingredient for brewers looking to create smooth, flavourful beers with an indulgent, silky finish.
entries.notes: Creamy, Nutty, Breakast Cereal Bar

entries.name: Heavily Peated Malt
entries.description:
Crafted for distillers who want bold, unmistakable smoke, Heavily Peated Malt (50-70ppm) brings a deeply phenolic character ideal for Islay-style single malts and smoky blends.

Rich aromas of tar and woodsmoke dominate the nose and carry through to the finish, layered atop a robust malt core. This is a malt that doesn’t shy away from its identity, lending bold flavour while retaining excellent conversion and yield.

Produced at the peating plant at our Tweed Valley Maltings, each batch is precisely targeted for phenol levels and consistency. It’s a favourite for any whisky that demands assertive smoke and a powerful finish.

entries.name: Imperial Malt
entries.description:
Imperial Malt is a bold, intensely kilned malt that delivers a deep amber to light brown hue (40-50 °EBC) and a rich, toasty malt complexity. It offers pronounced biscuit, toasted bread crust and nutty caramel notes.

It’s ideal for Bitters, Brown Ales and Porters, adding depth and structure to bring a warming, full-bodied mouthfeel to beers.

Compared to Munich Malt, Imperial Malt is darker and toastier, with a more robust biscuity intensity and a slight dry, nutty edge.

Best used at 5-30% in recipes to enhance body and malt richness, it can contribute bold malt character without excessive caramel sweetness, making it a go-to choice for deep, complex malt layers in most ales.
entries.notes: Biscuit Dry Sweetness (Honey/Plums), Bread Crust

entries.name: Lightly Peated Malt
entries.description:
Lightly Peated Malt brings a gentle wisp of smoke to your whisky, offering just enough phenolic character to enhance complexity without dominating the spirit.

At 5-15ppm, this malt is ideal for distillers seeking subtle peat notes – think soft bonfire smoke, earthy undertones and a whisper of medicinal phenols. The result is a refined balance where the malt’s sweetness and grain character can still shine through.

Perfect for Highlands-style whiskies, blends requiring a smoky dimension or for introducing a soft peat note to otherwise unpeated spirits. Made at our dedicated peating plant using finished white malt, the process ensures consistent phenol uptake and exceptional handling properties. A great option for distillers exploring nuance rather than intensity.

entries.name: Low Colour Golden Promise®™
entries.description:
Low Colour Golden Promise® Malt is a heritage malt that offers the same premium sweet, clean and slightly nutty malt character as traditional Finest Pale Ale Golden Promise®, but with a lighter colour (max 3.5 °EBC) for brewers seeking a paler, more delicate malt profile.

This makes it ideal for light, hop-forward styles such as Hazy IPAs, New England IPAs and crisp Golden Ales, where a soft malt backbone supports vibrant hop expression without adding too much colour or biscuity richness.

Compared to Finest Pale Ale Golden Promise, Low Colour Golden Promise is lighter in hue and slightly more fermentable, producing a crisper finish with less residual sweetness. Against Extra Pale Ale Malt, meanwhile, although similarly pale, Low Colour Golden Promise provides a more rounded, slightly sweeter profile, making it a great choice for brewers who want brightness without sacrificing malt character.

Furthermore, as we own the Golden Promise variety, supply seed through our agricultural merchanting division and purchase the barley direct from trusted growers each year, we can offer full traceability and sustainability data on the finished malt.
entries.notes: Light Malty

entries.name: Low Colour Maris Otter
entries.description:
Low Colour Maris Otter Malt delivers the same iconic biscuity depth and full-bodied character as Finest Pale Ale Maris Otter, but with a lighter colour (max 3.5 °EBC).

This makes it perfect for brewers seeking Maris Otter’s signature malty richness in paler styles like Golden Ales, Pale Ales, Hazy IPAs and New England IPAs, where malt complexity is desired without deepening the beer’s hue.

When comparing it to Low Colour Golden Promise, Low Colour Maris Otter has a more pronounced biscuit character and a touch more structure while, against Extra Pale Ale Malt, it offers more depth, making it an excellent choice for modern pale beers that still need a hint of malt complexity.
entries.notes: Rich Malty

entries.name: Malted Oats
entries.description:
Malted Oats bring a smooth, creamy mouthfeel with a delicate cereal sweetness, alongside a pale straw hue (2-4 °EBC).

Unlike Flaked Oats, malting enhances their enzymatic activity, allowing for easier mash conversion while still delivering the silky texture and haze stability. The velvety fullness allows it to take as many hops as you can throw at it for Hazy and/or Double IPAs, providing balance.

In more traditional usage, meanwhile, Malted Oats provides the backbone of creaminess in Oatmeal Stouts and Porters, smoothing the astringency that may result from the heavy use of roasted grains and adding a complexity of flavour.

Typically used at 5-20% in the grist, Malted Oats enhance body, foam stability and provide a rounded malt backbone, making them a great choice for brewers seeking a smooth, silky texture with a clean, light oat flavour in modern and traditional styles alike.
entries.notes: Creamy, Porridge Oat

entries.name: Malted Rye
entries.description:
Malted Rye is a highly functional, enzyme-active malt that delivers classic spicy, earthy rye character with a dry, crisp finish, alongside a warm copper hue (2-6 °EBC).

Understandably, Malted Rye is a key ingredient in Rye IPAs, where its distinct peppery spice and smooth texture add complexity. It’s also excellent in hoppy beer styles, with its spice complementing citrus hops.

Malted Rye has a clean profile and, compared to another ‘non-barley’ malt such as Wheat Malt, it provides a drier mouthfeel with a bold grainy bite.

Typically used at 10-50% in the grist – although if using at greater than 20%, rice husks are recommended to aid filtration – Malted Rye enhances spicy depth, improves foam stability and adds a signature dry finish. It is an essential choice for brewers looking to introduce Rye’s distinctive character while maintaining fermentability and balance in their beers.
entries.notes: Spicy

entries.name: Medium Peated Malt
entries.description:
Striking a balance between smoke and spirit, Medium Peated Malt delivers a confident but approachable phenolic profile at 20-40ppm.

Expect aromas of damp earth, smouldering wood and a measured medicinal edge, underpinned by a rich cereal backbone. This level of peat allows the distiller to build structure and smokiness into their whisky without overwhelming the malt character.

This makes it ideal for single malts with a pronounced yet drinkable peated style or for creating complexity in blended whiskies. The malt is peated post-kilning at our dedicated peating plant to maximise phenol absorption while preserving malt integrity.

For distillers aiming for a profile similar to classic island whiskies, this malt offers versatility and depth.

entries.name: Munich Malt
entries.description:
Munich Malt is a rich, deeply kilned malt that enhances beers with a warm amber hue (18-22 °EBC) and an intense malt complexity. It delivers deep biscuit, toasted bread and light caramel notes, making it an excellent choice for malt-forward styles like Bocks, Märzens, Dunkels and rich Amber Ales.

With a slightly higher residual sweetness than Vienna Malt, it provides a more pronounced malt backbone, adding depth and body without excessive caramelisation.

Compared to Vienna Malt, Munich is darker, fuller and more malty, bringing stronger toasty and biscuity notes. It can be used at 10-50% in recipes to boost malt complexity or even at 100% for robust, malt-driven beers.

Against higher-kilned malts like Imperial or Aromatic Malt, Munich is less intense but still impactful, offering rounded malt depth rather than sharp sweetness. It’s perfect for brewers looking to elevate malt richness while maintaining smooth drinkability.
entries.notes: Bready, Malty

entries.name: Pale Chocolate
entries.description:
Pale Chocolate Malt is a roasted malt that delivers smooth cocoa, mild coffee and toasted nut flavours, with a deep brown hue (530-665 °EBC).

It provides a gentle roast character without the acrid bitterness of darker roasted malts, meaning it can be a malt of choice for Porters, Stouts, Brown Ales and Milds, where chocolate depth with a rounded finish is desired.

Pale Chocolate is less sharp and bitter than standard Chocolate Malt. It contributes colour and complexity without being overpowering, making it perfect for up to 10% in the grist.

Brewers looking for subtle roastiness, refined chocolate character and a smooth, dry finish will find Pale Chocolate an excellent choice for crafting balanced, malt-forward dark beers.
entries.notes: Coffee Beans, Light Roasty

entries.name: Pot Still Distilling Malt
entries.description:
Pot Still Distilling Malt is crafted specifically for whisky production, delivering exceptional spirit yield, consistent performance and a clean, fermentable extract.

Our Pot Still Distilling Malt is produced from the highest quality two-row spring barley procured through our agricultural merchanting division, McCreath Simpson & Prentice, which means it is traceable back to the farm on which it was grown.

Pot Still Distilling Malt is malted to optimise enzymatic potential and carbohydrate availability, ensuring maximum alcohol yield per tonne while preserving a clean, cereal-forward flavour ideal for pot still distillation.

With a focus on fermentability and efficiency, Pot Still Distilling Malt offers a balanced protein content and a fine modification profile, making it perfectly suited for single malt and blended whisky production. It produces a bright, clear wort and supports a reliable, vigorous fermentation – key to achieving a refined, high-quality new make spirit.

Distillers can rely on Pot Still Distilling Malt to provide consistent extract performance and superior conversion, all while laying down a clean, neutral base for further flavour development through yeast, distillation and maturation.

entries.name: Premium English Caramalt
entries.description:
Premium English Caramalt is a rich, high-quality caramel malt that provides a deeper, more pronounced sweetness than standard Caramalt, with a golden-amber hue (54-66 °EBC).

It delivers smooth toffee, light caramel and honeyed notes, adding body and malt complexity while maintaining a clean, slightly dry finish. This makes it perfect for Pale Ales, Bitters and West Coast IPAs, where a balanced malt sweetness enhances drinkability.

Compared to our Caramalt, Premium English Caramalt is darker, fuller and provides a richer caramel flavour, yet remains less intense than our crystal malt range, which provide deeper caramelisation and raisin-like notes.

Typically used at 5-15% in grists, it enhances mouthfeel, malt depth and residual sweetness, making it an excellent choice for brewers wanting a silky caramel malt backbone without overpowering the final beer.
entries.notes: Horlicks, Shreddies, Sweet

entries.name: Red Rye Crystal
entries.description:
Red Rye Crystal is a speciality rye malt that delivers spicy rye and malty flavours, alongside a distinct deep red hue (237-310 °EBC), making it a great autumnal flavour for seasonal beers.

It adds body, mouthfeel and a signature rye spice, making it an excellent choice for Rye IPAs and Red Ales, where a warming, complex malt character is desired.

Compared to our standard Malted Rye, Red Rye Crystal is sweeter and richer, with some pronounced caramel and dark fruit notes, whereas regular Malted Rye is drier and more spicy.

It also differs from Crystal Dark, which is similar on scale in terms of colour, as it lacks rye’s distinctive peppery edge.

Typically used at 5-15% in the grist, Red Rye Crystal enhances depth, mouthfeel and colour, making it ideal for brewers looking to introduce sweet, malty rye complexity with a smooth, spicy finish to their beers.
entries.notes: Bread Crust, Malty, Sweet

entries.name: Roasted Barley
entries.description:
Roasted Barley is produced using unmalted barley, so enters the roasting drum without having gone through any of the steps of the conventional malting process. It is a highly roasted product that delivers bold, smoky and coffee-like flavours, along with a dark brown to black hue (1300-1900 °EBC).

It provides a dry, crisp finish with intense roasted bitterness, making it a key ingredient in Stouts – particularly Dry Stouts – Porters and other dark beers where robust, roasted flavours are desired.

Although the colour specification is very similar to Black Malt, Roasted Barley has a sharper, more pronounced roasted bitterness and a bolder coffee and burnt grain profile.

Typically used at 5-10% in the grist, Roasted Barley enhances colour and adds a distinctive dry, roasted edge, making it essential for brewers seeking intense, burnt flavours and a dry finish in dark beer styles.

entries.name: Simpsons DRC®
entries.description:
Simpsons DRC® is a malt exclusive to Simpsons Malt and is unique in that it undergoes the roasting process twice – hence the name Double Roasted Crystal!

This intensely crystalised malt delivers deep toffee, burnt sugar and subtle plum and raisin notes, along with a dark mahogany hue (280-320 °EBC), making it an ideal addition to Stouts, Porters, Barleywines and other robust ales, where a bold, layered malt character is desired.

Typically used at 5-15% in grists, Simpsons DRC® enhances mouthfeel, depth and residual sweetness, balancing roasted malts and hop bitterness while adding unparalleled richness and complexity to dark, full-bodied beers.
entries.notes: Dark Caramel, Subtle Taste of Plums & Raisins

entries.name: Torrefied Wheat
entries.description:
Torrefied Wheat is an unmalted adjunct created by rapidly heating raw wheat until it expands or 'pops', breaking down the cell walls and gelatinising starches.

This process makes its extract more accessible during mashing while preserving wheat’s high protein content. These proteins greatly enhance head retention, foam stability and mouthfeel, making Torrefied Wheat a valued addition in beers where a dense, lasting head and fuller body are needed.

Flavour-wise, it is neutral to lightly grainy, contributing structure rather than sweetness. Compared with Flaked Wheat, Torrefied Wheat tends to provide a crisper mouthfeel and improved foam stability, while Wheat Malt contributes more fermentable extract and bready, biscuity flavours.

Typically used at 5-25% of the grist, Torrefied Wheat is common in Pale Ales, Bitters, Stouts and Porters, as well as modern hazy styles, where it enhances texture and haze stability without overpowering the malt profile.
entries.notes: Neutral

entries.name: Very Heavily Peated Malt
entries.description:
For the peatiest of expressions, Very Heavily Peated Malt (80ppm+) delivers intense, enveloping smoke for every dram. Expect full-on phenolic impact with little room for subtlety.

This malt is the foundation of ultra-peated single malts, where phenol is not just an accent but the star. It creates whiskies with extreme character, long finishes and a cult following among peat lovers.

Despite its intensity, our controlled peating process ensures quality and consistency, using fully malted barley peated post-kilning for optimal phenol uptake. Best used with precision and purpose, this malt is for distillers pushing flavour boundaries and creating bold, unforgettable spirits.

entries.name: Wheat Malt
entries.description:
Wheat Malt is a highly functional, enzyme-rich malt that enhances head retention, body and mouthfeel, while contributing a delicate bready, doughy sweetness with subtle nutty undertones.

With a pale straw hue, it is essential in European wheat beers including Hefeweizens, Witbiers and Dunkelweizens, but also plays a supporting role in Pale Ales and IPAs, where it improves foam stability and adds texture.

Compared to Pale Ale or Lager Malts, Wheat Malt is higher in proteins and lacks husk, giving it a fuller body but requiring careful lautering.

German wheat beers require a minimum 50% Wheat Malt in the mash, but any more than 70% can cause brewhouse problems. So, in German styles, somewhere between 50-70% Wheat Malt is considered the norm, but this can be slightly less for wheat beer adaptations in the UK and North America.

It also benefits other modern craft beers though, adding silky mouthfeel, improved haze stability and a subtle, rounded malt character.
